clue.text: Depicting characters performing in play, or art

indicators.note: the letters (characters) are put to work in a new arrangement, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing actors at work in a stage play or in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters performing' signals that the letters of PLAY OR ART are shuffled; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or representation of someone is a portrayal, so the gerund used as a noun fits.

clue.text: Fruit, soft and well-rounded

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Describing a ripe piece of fruit that is soft and nicely round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes a body that is pleasantly fat or rounded out.

clue.text: King and two biblical characters free of duty

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A monarch and two figures from the Bible are let off their duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry or worker is to take over so they are released from duty.

clue.text: Account being overdrawn, had to move fast

indicators.note: the account is 'being' in the red, that is, sitting inside that colour word

parts.note: an overdrawn account is said to be in the red

explanation.surface: Someone whose bank balance went negative had to hurry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' works as the container signal: an overdrawn account is said to be in the red in British banking talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, to go at great speed, as one who had to hurry did.

clue.text: Keen, say, to make bets

indicators.note: the two words are used as raw material to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager, for instance, to place wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals rearranging the letters of KEEN SAY. A Yankee is a combination bet of eleven wagers on four horses, familiar in British betting shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a multiple wager in British bookmaking, covering every double, treble and accumulator on four selections.

clue.text: What could make a party go with a swing

definitions.text: What could make a party go with a swing

parts.words: What could make a party go with a swing
parts.note: a social party going with a swing is a lively one; a political party winning on a huge electoral swing has an overwhelming victory

explanation.surface: Asking what would make a social gathering go really well.
explanation.definitionFit: An election won by an enormous margin, after a big swing of votes, is called a landslide.

clue.text: Frenchman in a grubby vest

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A man from France wearing a dirty vest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'grubby' into 'vest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a typical French man's name, as in the designer Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Longed for time to take up study

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means writing it from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat room

explanation.surface: Someone long wanted the time to start studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' turns DEN to NED in this down clue; 'for' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long or pine for something, so both are past-tense verbs of desire.

clue.text: This military order looks fine

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it, so looks as a verb gives eyes
fine, as in 'that's fine', means all right

explanation.surface: A parade-ground command that seems perfectly good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' wants to be a noun about appearance; it is the verb, giving EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is the parade command to turn the head to the right in salute.

clue.text: People wanting a new landlord

parts.note: the public are people in general

explanation.surface: Tenants who would like a new landlord for their building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' here is the British sense: the person who runs a pub, not one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the keeper of a pub, licensed to sell drink, is called the landlord.

clue.text: Got close, earned review

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, here read as re-viewing the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Something came near and earned a write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' signals that EARNED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it, so neared means drew nearer.

clue.text: Add pages in a final section?

indicators.note: the pages are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: the end is the final part of anything

explanation.surface: Asking whether extra pages added in a closing section count as an appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the pages inside the other pieces. The question mark nods to an appendix, which is just such a final section.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or add something at the end of a text.

clue.text: Girl will entertain no alternative site for Hamlet

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Elsie is a girl's name
nor introduces the negative alternative in 'neither this nor that'

explanation.surface: A woman will play host to a man with nowhere else to stage his play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will entertain' signals a container. 'Hamlet' looks like a small village; it is Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore, the Danish castle at Helsingør, is where Shakespeare sets the tragedy of the prince.

clue.text: Yet one may be at one's lowest on them

definitions.text: Yet one may be at one's lowest on them

parts.words: Yet one may be at one's lowest on them
parts.note: the top parts of shoes, worn through to them

explanation.surface: A paradox: being on something high while at rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the clash of high and low; the uppers of worn-out shoes are all that remain when the soles are gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe uppers give the idiom for being destitute, when one's shoes are worn down to the uppers.

clue.text: Dog under piano consumes remnant of food

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece under another is written after it

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: the dog eats the remnant, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog
an end, as in a cigarette end, is what is left over

explanation.surface: A dog lying under a piano wolfs down scraps of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' signals the container and 'under' places the piano first in this down clue; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is an old word for provisions, especially fodder for animals.

clue.text: They may be found working in steamship at sea

indicators.note: being all at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors working aboard a steamer out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' signals that STEAMSHIP is rearranged; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow crew members working together on a ship are shipmates.

clue.text: Lively parties given by mum in lodgings

parts.note: mum, as in 'keep mum', means be quiet, which is sh
digs is British slang for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: Raucous gatherings thrown by a mother in a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother; it means silent, giving SH. DIGS is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a noisy, lively party.

clue.text: Love in the air? Stick around for marriage

indicators.note: the clinging word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to cling is to stick fast
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
up means aloft, in the air

explanation.surface: Romance is everywhere, so stay close for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; 'Love in the air' reads as romance but splits into zero and aloft. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupling is a joining of two, so a pairing in marriage qualifies.

clue.text: Used for hanging pirate captain on vessel?

indicators.note: the captain's name is placed on the vessel word, following it

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pirate was strung up aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a cooking pot. A pothook is the hook a pot hangs from over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothook is an S-shaped hook on which a cooking pot is suspended over a hearth.

clue.text: Greet us, perhaps, with a wave

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone might say hello to us by waving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that GREET US is rearranged; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the hand is one kind of gesture, a movement that conveys meaning.

clue.text: Gets satisfaction out of religious work

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works
the Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone finds fulfilment through church work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets satisfaction' sounds like contentment; it is the duel sense of demanding redress.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact satisfaction or revenge is to demand and obtain it from someone.

clue.text: Acquit a drunk, now living on water

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A drunk is cleared in court and now lives on a houseboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a noun for the defendant; it signals rearranging ACQUIT A. 'now' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic describes plants or animals that live in or on water.

clue.text: When people can look forward to retirement

definitions.text: When people can look forward to retirement

parts.words: When people can look forward to retirement
parts.note: retirement suggests stopping work, but retiring also means going to bed for the night

explanation.surface: Speaking of the age at which workers can expect a pension.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours at which people go to sleep each night are when they retire.

clue.text: Reasons for which people fight

definitions.meaning: grounds or motives for something to happen
principles or movements that campaigners struggle for

explanation.surface: Explaining why people go to war.
explanation.definitionFit: Causes are both the reasons behind events and the ideals people champion.

clue.text: A young animal has it in some measure

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, fox or lion

explanation.surface: A baby animal possesses something to a certain degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some measure' looks like 'to some extent'; it is an old unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit is an ancient unit of length, roughly the forearm from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Call up a woman, a case for approval

indicators.note: the woman forms a case, an outer container, for the other piece

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Ringing a woman to argue that something deserves to be approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a case for' signals that the woman's name wraps round the sign of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to summon or bring it to mind.

clue.text: Expert — for a doctor, nothing to it

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A doctor finds a skilled procedure easy, saying there is nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, especially with the hands.

clue.text: Prepare for take-off?

parts.note: take-off suggests an aircraft, but here it is taking off clothing

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a plane to leave the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the fastenings of a jacket readies it to be removed.

clue.text: Travel after star of film and TV

definitions.meaning: to journey, especially a long, hard way

definitions.text: after star of film and TV
definitions.meaning: the word that follows Star in the science-fiction franchise title

explanation.surface: A screen celebrity goes on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity; it is the first word of the title Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long arduous journey, and Star Trek is the space series.

clue.text: In some respect a clever presentation

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that something is, in one sense, a smart show.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show or display put on for viewers.
